title: Progressive cut-tier playbook and release-notes orchestration for API / Console / Runtime
creator: Maya Chen
background: We need a compact, decision-ready playbook that defines progressive 'cut tiers' for our combined API / Console / Runtime release train and a tightly coordinated release-notes workflow so cross-functional teams can make fast, consistent scope decisions during the last 4 weeks before launch.
goal: Create a reproducible gating matrix and communications cadence that reduces last-minute scope churn, aligns cut decisions across engineering/design/support/sales, and produces a single authoritative release-notes artifact ready for public and internal channels.
milestones: T-28: Feature freeze candidate list published (authors + owners)
T-21: Integration & system smoke test window opens
T-14: Cut-tier review 1 (soft cut) — non-blocking regressions required to remain
T-7: Cut-tier review 2 (conservative cut) — only P0/critical fixes accepted
T-3: Final freeze (hard cut) — emergency-only exceptions via Operations Board
Launch Day: Release notes finalization and publication; post-launch incident pager rotation
cut_tiers: Soft cut (T-14): Flatten low-risk changes; allowed: docs, minor UX polish, telemetry tweaks. Must have green e2e and owner sign-off.
Conservative cut (T-7): Only P0/P1 bug fixes and rollout safety features. New feature toggles allowed if behind default-off.
Hard cut (T-3): No code merges except critical fixes triaged by Release Lead and reviewed by SRE/QA. All PRs require explicit exception approval.
Emergency cut (post T-0): Hotfix protocol via on-call rotation; customer impact assessments and immediate comms required.
cut_criteria: Classification: Every PR/change must be labeled with risk (low/medium/high) and type (feature/bugfix/docs/telemetry).
Quality gates: Unit tests + CI pass; no new e2e failures attributable to the change; performance delta <= 5% for critical paths.
Operational readiness: Metrics dashboard and tracing hooks must be present for new surface area; rollout canary plan defined for >0.5% traffic changes.
Security/compliance: Any change touching private deployments, RBAC, or encryption requires security_review_required=true and approval before merge.
release_notes_plan: Owner: Product (PM) owns final artifact; each feature owner supplies a 1-2 sentence blurb + user impact + migration notes by T-14.
Template: Single canonical release-notes template (public summary, detailed developer notes, breaking changes, upgrade steps, known issues).
Coordination: Weekly sync between PMs, Docs, SDK, DevRel starting T-28. Docs publishes draft at T-14; legal/security review complete by T-7.
Channels: Public notes (docs.redwood.com/release), internal TLDR for Sales/Support, SDK changelogs, in-console spotlight updates.
stakeholders: Product: Release Lead (PM) — decision authority for release-notes and cut approvals
Engineering: API, Runtime, Console leads — technical gating and rollout safety plans
SRE: Service SLO validation and rollout guards
Design/Docs: User-facing copy and in-console messaging
DevRel/Sales/Support: GTM enablement and customer-facing comms
Legal/Security: Compliance sign-off for private deployment changes
communication_plan: Daily triage channel (Slack #release-train) during T-7..T+3 with pinned decision log
Weekly cross-functional reviews T-28..T-14; then daily standups T-7..Launch
Decision log: Every cut/exception must be recorded in the Release Decisions doc with owner, rationale, and rollback conditions
Release notes draft: Docs posts link in #release-train at T-14; PM collects approvals by T-7
rollout_strategy: Canary-first: New runtime optimizations roll out to canary pool (1-2% traffic) for 24–48 hours with automated rollback on SLO violation
Feature flags: All new API/Console features behind flags with progressive exposure; SDKs receive opt-in preview builds
Region-aware ramp: Stagger region expansion (us-west -> us-east -> eu-central) with manual gates between regions for stateful migrations
rollback_criteria: Latency regression >20% on p95 sustained for >10 minutes
Error volume increase >3x baseline for 5 minutes with customer-visible failures
Data correctness or loss incidents affecting >0.1% of requests
Security incident or unauthorized access detected
risks: Late-breaking runtime performance regressions require cross-team debugging and may force scope rollback
Incomplete release-notes blur responsibilities between Docs and PM resulting in delayed public comms
Private deployment changes (KMS/HSM) may incur longer legal/security cycles if surfaced late

Define exception approval flow and RACI for Release Board — owner: Liam (due T-24)
Implement PR labeling automation to surface risk/type — owner: Eng infra (due T-26)

Publish SDK changelog checklist for DevRel — owner: Alex (due T-10)
acceptance_criteria: A documented cut-tier matrix with explicit decision owners and approval steps published to Confluence
Release-notes template in docs repo and sample completed for the upcoming release by T-7
Automation in CI to enforce labeling and quality gates for T-14 onwards
Stakeholder sign-off recorded (PM, Eng leads, SRE, Docs, Legal) before hard cut
notes: This playbook prioritizes a bias toward safe launches while enabling targeted feature transfers via flags. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc exceptions and centralize the decision trail to speed post-launch analysis.
